findings.highlight: At the end…
findings.evidenceJa: 最後に
findings.governingReading: Finally / at the last threshold.
findings.explanation: The temporal phrasing makes the final recurrence sound like an ordinary sequence endpoint.

findings.highlight: her days were filled with neglect even from her trusted knights
findings.evidenceJa: 信頼できる[ruby text="と"]騎[ruby text="も"]士たちから疎まれるようになった日々
findings.governingReading: Days when even the trusted knights/companions came to shun her.
findings.explanation: The relational ruby and active estrangement become vague neglect.

findings.highlight: Arturia was made to wish for a battle she did not wish for
findings.evidenceJa: 望まぬ戦いを望まれたアルトリア
findings.governingReading: Arturia was called upon to fight wars she did not desire.
findings.explanation: The demand imposed on the king is reassigned as her contradictory wish.

findings.highlight: To start at the end
findings.evidenceJa: 結論から言えば
findings.governingReading: To state the conclusion first.
findings.explanation: A standard discourse marker becomes an internally awkward phrase.

findings.highlight: The end final battle of King Arthur.
findings.evidenceJa: アーサー王の最期である
findings.governingReading: It is King Arthur’s end / final moments.
findings.explanation: The line is grammatically broken and narrows her end into a battle label.

findings.highlight: the only ones standing in the end were her and Mordred
findings.evidenceJa: 息子であ[ruby text="　モ"]る[ruby text="ード"]騎[ruby text="レッ"]士[ruby text="ト　"]だけだった
findings.governingReading: Only she and the knight who was her son—Mordred—remained.
findings.explanation: The layered identification of Mordred as both son and knight disappears.

findings.highlight: a fatal wound
findings.evidenceJa: もはや癒せない傷
findings.governingReading: a wound that could no longer be healed
findings.explanation: The translation promotes incurability into an explicit fatal diagnosis.

findings.highlight: Every one of her twelve battles was severe, and this just happened to be the greatest wound appropriate for her end
findings.evidenceJa: 十二もの戦はそのどれもが身を[ruby text="さ"]削くような戦いであり、これは、その最後に相応しい、もっとも大きな傷痕
findings.governingReading: All twelve battles wore away at her body; this was the greatest scar, fitting for the last of them.
findings.explanation: The bodily image is flattened and unsupported chance is added to the culmination.

findings.highlight: She returned to Britain her territory and destroyed her own army
findings.evidenceJa: ブリテンに戻り、自国の軍を蹴散らし
findings.governingReading: Returning to Britain, she routed her own country’s army.
findings.explanation: The sentence is malformed in one supplied text branch and blurs the parallel actions.

findings.highlight: The lone king, who tried to be a king until her last moments
findings.evidenceJa: 最期まで王として有り続けようとした独りの騎士
findings.governingReading: The lone knight who tried to remain king to the very end.
findings.explanation: The knight/king dual identity central to Saber’s characterization is collapsed.

findings.highlight: It must be more painful for you right now
findings.evidenceJa: 今は俺なんかより、セイバーの方が辛いだろう
findings.governingReading: Right now it must be harder for you than for someone like me.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s dismissive ranking of his own suffering disappears.

findings.highlight: It is only natural for me to protect you until you get better
findings.evidenceJa: マスターの傷が癒えるまでは、私が守るのは当然でしょう
findings.governingReading: It is natural that I protect my Master until his wounds heal.
findings.explanation: Saber’s explicit role language is generalized into second-person care.

findings.highlight: I need to sleep as well
findings.evidenceJa: 私とて、睡眠をとらなければ保てない身ですから
findings.governingReading: Even this body of mine cannot sustain itself without sleep.
findings.explanation: The bodily and ontological phrasing is reduced to an ordinary need.

findings.highlight: I let Saber take care of me
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーの看病を見守った
findings.governingReading: I watched over Saber’s nursing.
findings.explanation: Attentive observation becomes permission, changing Shirou’s stance and agency.

findings.highlight: she really is feminine
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーは本当に女の子だった
findings.governingReading: Saber truly was a girl.
findings.explanation: A concrete perception of her girlhood becomes an abstract gendered quality.

findings.highlight: She looks so lovely that it doesn’t seem like she would be capable of fighting
findings.evidenceJa: 倒れれば立ち上がれそうにないほど可憐だと思う
findings.governingReading: She seems so delicate that, if she fell, she might never rise again.
findings.explanation: The ominous image of being unable to rise is omitted.

findings.highlight: Then, she smiles faintly
findings.evidenceJa: 俺にとってはあまりにも儚げに、彼女は笑った
findings.governingReading: To me, her smile looked unbearably fragile.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s subjective and extreme response becomes a neutral manner adverb.

findings.highlight: She didn’t know happiness or entertainment
findings.evidenceJa: 喜びを知らず、満足な楽しみなど知らなかったクセに
findings.governingReading: Though she knew no joy, no satisfying pleasure.
findings.explanation: A condition of never knowing fulfilling enjoyment is recast as unfamiliarity with entertainment.

findings.highlight: I’m going mad. I really feel like I’m crazy
findings.evidenceJa: 気が触れる
findings.governingReading: I lose my senses—and then truly feel I may go mad.
findings.explanation: The staged loss of control becomes repetitive generic English.

findings.highlight: It’s okay. Listen, you have to smile for your own sake
findings.evidenceJa: もういい。いいから、自分の為に、笑わないと
findings.governingReading: Enough. Just— you have to smile for your own sake.
findings.explanation: A pressured interruption is turned into reassurance.

findings.highlight: I want her to know normal happiness
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーに人間らしい楽しみを知ってもらいたい
findings.governingReading: I want Saber to know human, ordinary enjoyment.
findings.explanation: The human-life contrast is generalized into happiness.

findings.highlight: you have to find your own happiness
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーが幸せにならないなんて嘘だ
findings.governingReading: It would be a lie for Saber not to become happy.
findings.explanation: Shirou’s characteristic truth/falsehood judgment becomes a generic obligation.

findings.highlight: Whayou are still talking about that?
findings.evidenceJa: な何を言うかと思えば、まだ、そんな事を言うのですか、貴方は
findings.governingReading: W-What are you saying? Are you still saying such things?
findings.explanation: The stammer and rebuke collapse into malformed English.

findings.highlight: She’s weak
findings.evidenceJa: 引き離そうとするセイバーの力が、弱い
findings.governingReading: The strength with which Saber tries to pull away is weak.
findings.explanation: A local change in her resistance is converted into a judgment that Saber herself is weak.

findings.highlight: I’ll let you go if you don’t love me
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーが俺じゃ駄目だって言うんなら、このまま手を離す
findings.governingReading: If you say I will not do for you, I will let go now.
findings.explanation: The source asks whether Shirou himself is unacceptable; the English asserts that her answer concerns reciprocal love.

findings.highlight: You knew my past, but you continued to invade me
findings.evidenceJa: 私の過去を知って、私の中に何度も入ってきた
findings.governingReading: You learned my past and entered inside me again and again.
findings.explanation: Dream-memory entry becomes a continuous hostile invasion and loses the repeated-event construction.

findings.highlight: I want to be with you, Saber
findings.evidenceJa: 俺はもっと、ずっとセイバーと一緒にいたい
findings.governingReading: I want to be with you more—always.
findings.explanation: The comparative and continuing duration of Shirou’s wish disappear.
